content.text:
1. Verdict: hybrid — with `person` as the default.

Hybrid must be an explicit deployment policy, not a runtime guess:

- B2B/workspace bot: mint `person`.
- Consumer/product bot: optionally mint provisional `$member`.
- Existing identity always wins regardless of type. The resolver already supports this cleanly: [entity-link-upsert.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:319).

2. “Isn’t every user our user?”

Yes, but not every user is the customer organization’s member.

“Uses a Lobu-powered bot,” “has a Lobu account,” and “belongs to tenant X” are three different facts. `$member` represents the third. It is org-scoped and security-bearing.

If Lobu eventually needs a platform-global user concept, introduce `$user` or rely on the auth `user`. Do not overload tenant `$member`.

3. Minting `$member` on chat is right when:

- The bot is itself the product, not an employee/CRM interface.
- A verified direct message explicitly constitutes registration.
- The chatter needs preferences, entitlements, quotas, or lifecycle state before web login.
- Every accepted chatter genuinely belongs to that bot’s product tenant.
- It is a one-to-one interaction. Never mint members from Slack channel enumeration, group participation, mentions, imported audiences, or arbitrary webhook authors.

Examples: a consumer coach, personal assistant, paid Telegram service.

4. Person-first is right when:

- The org represents a company or team.
- Chatters may be customers, leads, vendors, applicants, community members, or spam.
- Slack/GitHub audience graphs discover people who have never joined Lobu.
- The bot participates in groups or shared channels.
- Membership carries roles, seats, directory visibility, workspace access, or compliance meaning.

That is the correct model for `lobu-crm` and the normal Slack/WhatsApp support case. Current Slack/GitHub ACL behavior already follows it: unknown audience members become `person`, while identity resolution remains type-agnostic.

5. Concrete Lobu default

Default every connection to:

```text
audience_model = contacts
first chat → person
```

Allow an explicit bot-level override:

```text
audience_model = consumer_members
qualifying direct chat → $member(status=provisional)
```

Do not make this an org-wide heuristic based on channel name or whether the sender appears “user-like.”

Keep Telegram/Slack currently minting `person` by default in [sender-identity.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/gateway/connections/sender-identity.ts:40).

6. Exact hybrid lifecycle

| State | Entity | `auth_user_id` | Meaning | UI |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| B2B first chat | `person` | None | Contact/observed human | People/Contacts |
| Consumer first direct chat | `$member`, `status=provisional` | None | Chat-only product principal | Chat users, not Team |
| Admin invitation | `$member`, `status=invited` | None | Explicit workforce membership intent | Team → Pending invites |
| Verified login/join | `$member`, `status=active` | Required, trusted `auth:signup` | Actual authenticated tenant member | Team/Members; counts for seats |
| Removed membership | soft-deleted or explicit disabled state | Retained for audit, unusable for access | Former member | Former/disabled, not active lists |

Promotion rules:

- `person → active $member`: only after verified org membership. Preserve the canonical entity ID by promoting in place where possible.
- If an invited `$member` already exists, merge the person into that member deterministically.
- `provisional → active`: attach the trusted `auth_user_id` and retain the same entity.
- Never attach `auth_user_id` merely because a Telegram/Slack identifier was supplied by a client.
- Never treat `provisional` as a Better Auth membership or grant web/API roles.

Current code only supports `active | invited`; hybrid consumer mode therefore requires adding `provisional` and enforcing its semantics. See [member-entity-type.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/utils/member-entity-type.ts:85).

The existing invite implementation is correct: invited members have no `auth_user_id` until acceptance, specifically to avoid privilege takeover. See [auth/index.tsx](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:483) and [member-entity.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/utils/member-entity.ts:32).

One current gap: Slack “takeover” moves the platform identity from `person` to `$member`; it does not truly reuse or merge the original person entity. Historical references may remain split. See [subject-identities.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/server/src/auth/subject-identities.ts:100). Fix that before claiming seamless login-later reuse.

UI rules:

- Team directory: `active` and `invited`, with separate sections.
- Chat Users: `provisional`.
- Contacts/People: `person`.
- Seat counts: authenticated Better Auth membership, not entity type alone.
- The generic Memory `$member` list currently filters only by type, so it would be polluted without status filtering: [memory-browse.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/owletto/src/lib/memory-browse.ts:331).
- `organization.listMembers` already returns real Better Auth members and should remain the source for authorization/roles: [use-members.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/tg-person-mint/packages/owletto/src/hooks/use-members.ts:28).

7. Risks

- Always `$member`: turns spam and ambient channel participants into principals; corrupts directories, seats, roles, invitation semantics, and analytics; creates dangerous ambiguity between entity membership and actual Better Auth membership.
- Always person-until-login: weak fit for true chat-native products; requires promotion/merge; pre-login preferences and entitlements need identity-based handling.
- Hybrid: more states, filters, migrations, and test cases. A wrongly configured bot misclassifies users. Mitigate with one explicit audience policy and centralized minting/promotion logic.

8. Confidence: 94/100.

The only material uncertainty is whether Lobu wants `$member` to remain strictly synonymous with tenant membership. If yes, even consumer chatters should remain `person` until registration, and a separate `$user`/`participant` type is cleaner than provisional `$member`.
